newsitem.title: USA: Timken buys UK Torrington's aerospace unit. [CORRECTED 19:45 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Timken buys UK Torrington's aerospace unit. [CORRECTED 19:45 GMT]

text.p: Timken Co said Wednesday it bought Ingersoll-Rand Co unit Torrington Co Ltd's aerospace bearing operations for an undisclosed price (corrects to show Torrington is not privately-held but a unit of Ingersoll-Rand).
Timken said the unit, which is located in Wolverhampton, Great Britain, employs 100 people and posted less than $10 million in sales last year.

"We are committed to increasing our presence and range of products to customers in the European aerospace market, said chief executive Joseph Toot in a statement. "Part of our strategy to grow and improve customer service is to manufacture locally."

The company said the bearing operations will function as a unit of its subsidiary MPB Corp in Keene, N.H. The unit's operations manager Gary Kenmir and his management team will continue to run the day-to-day operations.
